utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. We will not keep you long this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on behalf of the Defence, I would like to congratulate our American friends. Their biggest holiday, the independence day. That's all from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Scott. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, my thanks to counsel as well for those good wishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you -- let me see. Few questions following on from where we left off yesterday in terms of your report. Sir, I'm hesitating, sir, because I'm going to try in the course of the afternoon just to move rather quickly, if possible, and maybe doing some, if you will, editing of my own notes as we go. So ... If you have your -- the stack of exhibits from yesterday, if you don't have those, perhaps the usher can assist in putting those in front of you again, the ones, the various charts and maps, starting with Exhibit 403, please. Can we start please, if you'll direct your attention to Exhibit 407 in that stack? I'm not sure whether on direct or cross-examination we spent much time looking at that yesterday. Yes, that's it. I see you have it there. Just primarily, sir, so that I can understand the exhibit and hopefully the Judges as well, as I understand, in looking a bit at this diagram, since yesterday, or map, this represents where the various places where the Croatian population was located in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the colour coding indicating concentration of the Croat population in Bosnia-Herzegovina as of 1991. Is that -- do I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You understand correctly, not a different -- not the different density, but the share of this population in the total number of inhabitants in Bosnia and Herzegovina. For particular municipalities, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So, for example, to use a municipality that we are all more or less familiar with, Mostar, it is one of the -- whatever you like to say, brightest red or darkest red colours indicating a high concentration or at least a high number, excuse me, a high number of Croats living in that area as opposed for instance we looked at yesterday, Foca, which is completely yellow. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But this map, just so again, so we can properly consider it in the future, this map says nothing about ratios or percentages but simply gives absolute numbers of Croats in these areas; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I did not have the same ambition that you have for this map. This is just a representation of some sizes. If the municipalities were different, then the map would also look different. So it is not sufficient to use a map and just a map as argument for --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the demographic point of view, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were telling us yesterday about some of the issues involved with demographic data for various municipalities, in particular Mostar, and the city of Mostar and you were raising some issues about that. Now, do I understand correctly that it's also true that there is no separate 1991 data for what might be called the old city, the Stari Grad, or the central district of Mostar, specifically? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the table that I showed you yesterday, that I would have to search for, I have forgotten my glasses, but I understand your question very well, and I'll try to answer it. The city of Mostar, like any other city, grows all the time. That is why the territorial scope of any city has to be changed. The statistics were lagging behind in monitoring the development of the city of Mostar, and it lagged behind by almost 50 years. It is very possible, and very easy to obtain the data based on the census of population for every family, every household, every part of every village for a cluster of villages, in our jargon we used to call it local communes. However --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, let me just take you back do my question. Again as in yesterday by question sometime maybe more -- my ambitions may be more basic than yours, if you'll allow me. I'm just simply asking you if you know, and if it's not something you looked at you can just tell us that, but just again looking at the Mostar city demographics or statistics, can you confirm is it correct that there is also no separate set of figures, as opposed to the overall city as previously defined. There is no separate figures for the central city or for what some people would call the old city, primarily Muslim part of the city? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that when you say Stari Grad, you refer to five neighbourhoods that have composed that part since 1953. Such data can be found for 1953, 1981 and 1993 in the yearbooks that were published after the censuses in 1953, 1981 and 1993. I have quite a lot of professional objections to the 1991 census, but I do accept such data as better than any other data that were collected in that state after the year 1991, so it is possible to find the data in the yearbook, and I can provide you with the number of that yearbook, and I could find the data with the grain of doubt as to the credibility of the census as a whole, because the census was prepared by one government and carried out by a different government, is not complete because it did not follow through the legal procedure. It can be used but all the sources relative to that census have to be compensated upon in the way I have just commented upon them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, if I could have the usher's assistance, I'd like to have you handed and to distribute in the courtroom what was previously marked and used in previously in the trial as P109.1 and P109.2. I'll tell the courtroom just, sorry for any confusion, the numbers are on the B/C/S original versions of the documents and not on the top pages. So actually I've just been shown there is also a marking on the English version as well. So I'm corrected on that. You might also see a bigger number on the B/C/S version so if I could have the usher's assistance give one of these to the witness and then distribute them to the Chamber and the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if I can direct your attention first, please, to 109.1, an excerpt of statistical compilation related to the 1991 census, 109.1 and if I can direct your attention to what would be page 300 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We were short.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There should have been at least one for the Judges, one for the registry and one for each Defence team I thought, but if a we miscounted, my apology. I'm sure it was my fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The question, in any event, counsel, will be I think short, I think. Looking first of all to 109.1, sir, page 300, I'll represent to you that these are the listings in the left column are municipalities, and you will see here in about roughly halfway down the column, the municipality of Mostar, and you will see the breakdown of the principal ethnic groupings, the first being -- the first number -- there is a total number then the first number being Croats and then Muslims and Serbs. And below the number, the first number in that line then there is another number below would you agree with me that that is a percentage, so that, for instance the total population in Mostar according to the 1991 census was approximately 126.628, the Muslim -- excuse me, the Croat population was approximately 43.037, the Muslim population was approximately 43.856, and the population -- and the percentages below there being Croat, 33.99, and Muslim 34.63. That's the same basically, even though the issues, excuse me, despite the issues you've raised about the 1991 census, those are essentially the same figures that you've used, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct. There were no other sources but the reservations remain. Not only reservations but the practice, the procedure, used during the census which followed the recommendations of the population commission of the United Nations, this commission has provided for the recommendations to be followed for one's national census to be complete, final, or in other words, official, because these recommendations are binding upon member states in order to be able to use the census data for demographic and other analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me next take you to the next of the charts that were just given to you, 109.2, page 182. Now, if you have page 182, you will see toward the upper part of the page, in the far left column, the heading, "Mostar." Which I hope you will agree with me that is the municipality of Mostar. And then below that, the series of names below that, are towns, cities or villages in the municipality of Mostar, so if you go toward the end of that column you will find, fourth from the bottom, the city of Mostar. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And these pages would have originally been laid out continuously across a bigger page or -- well, bigger or smaller but in any event, one continuous page, so if you turn to the next page, 183, you will see then again the fourth line from the bottom, the 1991 figures, again specifically for the city, as opposed to the municipality of Mostar, and what would be line, I believe line 39, 21.795 Croats and 25.929 Muslims, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says here, but in my expert study, I dealt with this problem. If you wish, I can give you the whole story about this data that you have just shown me because I actually was the one who helped these data being published, so that everybody can have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Professor let me just, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, Mr. Scott, for my interruption. I believe that with regard to the last thing that the professor said, that he helped for this -- for the data to be published, I believe that it would be very useful for the Honourable Chamber to hear what the professor has to say, because the professor wanted to say that these data are not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness -- witness, in your testimony you said that "because I actually was the one who helped this data being published, so that everybody can have them," right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We just want to hear how you helped this data being published.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the settlements that were covered by the statistics, to which settlements I added seven more settlements and then the data for these seven settlements were also published. I was talking about the methodology, I was talking about somebody's omission, either intentionally or unintentionally. I was talking about an omission, according to which only some data were published, and some were not. If we add one set of figures to another set of figures, the picture is completely different. This is what the signatories of these data know. One of them is professor Jakov Gelo, who is the director and now working in Zagreb and Hasan Zoric, the other one, an expert, my colleague, whom I both asked and told them that it would be very valuable for us in Bosnia-Herzegovina to publish the data on the national breakdown per settlements because that would be useful for many people. It would dispel the one picture on the mononational structure of Bosnia and Herzegovina because if the -- if the picture is different, then it is less danger that it will be distorted. So if you agree, I can illustrate that with a picture, and I can use the same example that we have been using so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, if the Prosecutor needs the data in your hands, he will ask you to put it on the ELMO and show us. Mr. Scott, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Professor I think I do understand. I don't pretend to be a demographer, but I think I do understand the point you were making yesterday and it's not necessary for you to repeat it again. Your view is, as I understand it, that the number that I just referred you to -- the numbers that I just referred you to would be substantially different if other -- if different boundaries of the city of Mostar were used. I understand that point. And again, my questions to you are much more basic than that. These numbers, these statistical numbers --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not municipal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the city, sir. In the city. Again my ambitions are more basic than yours. The Chamber has seen some of these statistics before and I just wanted to make sure that whether you agree with them or not we were starting at least could start from the same base. That those are the numbers I've just shown you Exhibit 109.1 and 109.2 come from the 1991 census and subject to the issues you've raised, those are the numbers that basically you and all other demographers have essentially used, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Again, I repeat with some reservations as to the objectivity of the census, which was not completed, but these data are the best there are available but what you are reading now is just one part of the city. Those who look at the figures don't have to be demographers, not to agree with the set of data that you're showing us because the city is five times bigger than it is represented by these figures, and the statistics covered only one fifth of the city. I believe that I've made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think you were clear before, sir, thank you. Let me ask you, however, on that very point, isn't it your testimony, sir, that the phenomenon, if I can call it, that that you've described or the error that you claim existed, that goes back to sometime before 1960, doesn't it? This error or as you called it, occurred in the 1961 census, the 1971 census and again in the 1981 census, correct? Assuming there was an error, it also occurred in those other censuses?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I said yesterday and I repeat it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So this situation, sir, is a result of a structure and system that was put in place some 30 plus years earlier by the prior communist government and was not something that was put in place by the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina after the referendum in 1992, was it?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you said. I did say that it was a mistake. Whose mistake it was, I don't know, and why.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So we can agree, can we -- can't we, that assuming again that you're correct that this error was made, this was not a manipulation made by any what might be called a Muslim government but was something that had been occurring for many decades under the prior administration, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what is correct, but if the errors are abused or used by the people who do not understand them, then these people will use them in any way they want, in political, social or any other terms. That is why the errors of this nature, which carry some national attributes have not been helpful for the city of Mostar, and hence their possible manipulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, sir, on that -- in that regard, let me go to the three sources of -- if I understood you well, the three sources of data that you said you used for post-1991 comparisons and if I heard you correctly, the first one you made reference to was a refugee office and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. could you give us a bit more specifics on what refugee office that was?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you will allow me I just need to find this, because I wanted to quote exactly the thing that I said yesterday. This is the office for refugees whose full name is the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, the refugee office in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, that was partly the question that I wanted to ask you. That was the first source you indicated. The second source you gave, and forgive me if I didn't get exactly everything accurate in my notes, but I believe you said the municipal welfare office in Mostar for data in 1994 and 1995, and then the third source that you gave was the department for social welfare in Mostar through a series of dates you gave us in 1994. And my question to you, sir, is just simply this: All those sources or agencies or sources of the government of the Croatian Republic of -- either the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna or the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what is correct, but I can show you what I used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... all those agencies, all those sources were agencies of the HVO government, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems that you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, before we leave -- I think we are about to finish with these diagrams but if I could direct your attention to Exhibit 409, and the three rows of charts --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, looking it at the last row, the multi--- if you will, the multicoloured row from the 1961, 1971, 1981 and 1991, sir, whatever else we have talked about in the last two days, would you not agree with me that at the very least, what this document clearly shows is that at no time since at least 1961, was the municipality of Mostar or the city of Mostar -- let me stop there. Do you understand this to be the city or municipality of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I have to go back to what I have already said, and that is what I deem very important. My first sentence was that Bosnia-Herzegovina regarded today as a state follows the national division.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask my learned friend not to be impatient. The professor is not used to talking in front of a Chamber, and he is not allowed to give his full answer. I would kindly ask the Chamber to allow him to provide his explanations and I don't see any reason for this impatience. The professor has to be allowed to give his explanations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, I believe that the Prosecutor asked you a very simple question. Do you understand this to be the city or the municipality of Mostar? This is also what we want to know, the answer to this question. You answer that question first. If you need some explanations, you could do that. And if the Prosecutor wants more information in this area, he will ask for more information from you. We just want to hear what is relevant to this case. Yes. You may answer this question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer is in the title and in the caption beneath every figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I apologise, sir, regretfully I don't read your language and these were not provided in translation. If you can just assist us, please, when the Mostar that is referred on Exhibit 409 or I should say D1/409, does that indicate the city of Mostar or the municipality of Mostar? Just please help us with that.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are districts and municipalities, depending on the year. On the other hand, this is Mostar in Austro-Hungarian times, in Yugoslav times and in the present time. How can I answer your question in simple terms the way you expect me to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me -- all right. Let me try to make it even simpler then, sir. Directing your attention only to the last row of figures, starting with 1961. We won't look at the others above that for now. As to that row of figures, can you just please tell us, is this chart depicting the municipality of Mostar, the opstina of Mostar, or the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Municipality of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me go back to the question that I began to put to you before, and my apologies for needing to clarify it in somewhat mid-sentence I had to ask for your clarification but, sir, won't you agree with me that whatever else we may argue about, at least since 1961, there has clearly been no substantial Croat majority in Mostar at any time?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear in this illustration so what you're saying is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, both in your -- sorry, forgive me again. To finish up on the maps and I think we will be done with the maps, if I could have the usher's assistance please to distribute what's been marked as P947 both to the witness, please, and to counsel, and the Chamber? Sir, if you can look at that for a moment and I'll represent to you, sir, for the record and tell the Chamber and of course of additional evidence has to be presented on this, I will, this has been prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor and make that very clear to you, and I'll also tell you that -- how the map on the right was prepared. Just so know that but I think when you compare I think when I put my question to you I think you'll see that it's a relatively straightforward --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank my learned friend, I'm sure he expected my question so I would kindly ask my learned friend to tell us what the source of these maps is, who compiled these maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think Mr. Prosecutor has already said that. He said that this has been prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you have more information to furnish to the Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can provide a bit more. The Office of the Prosecutor is fortunate enough to have some in-house demographic expertise. There are I believe if I'm not mistaken two people on the OTP staff who are demographers and I can represent to the Chamber that the map on the left side of the page has been prepared from exactly the same 1991 census data that we have talked about for the last two days. The map on the right side of the page for 1997, since there is no census data after the war, is based upon voter registration information. Clearly not the same as a census. No attempt to so indicate. But it is some data that's available across all the three main ethnic groups, in terms of voter registration information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, again sir, my question is a very basic one, if you can pull out your Exhibit D1/406 and maybe just put those -- these two exhibits side by side, looking at your Exhibit 406 and the map on the right side of Exhibit 947, with a few differences sir would you not agree with me that they are roughly quite similar?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the quantity and quality of the sources which were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course it does, but if you look at the bright blue colour, for instance, on Exhibit 947 for 1997, you look at that bright blue information and compare it to your whatever you like to call it, red or bright orange, dark orange information on your 406, don't those areas look quite similar?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is another difference that you haven't mentioned. One is 1996 and the other is 1997. My map was made in 1996 and yours was made in 1997. When I was interpreting my map yesterday, I told you that the one from 1996 is -- does not reflect the current situation. I mentioned Bosansko Grahovo and Glamoc and Vrdar municipalities and I referred to the return of the refugees and I said that they probably are coloured differently. I'm sure they are not red, though. Another thing that would be useful --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, I don't think you understand the question put to you by the Prosecutor. Mr. Scott, you may repeat your question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm simply asking you, and again my question is very basic, I think. If you look at the two maps side by side, your Exhibit D1/406 and the map depicted on the right side, P947 are quite similar, aren't they. The bright blue areas, the Croatian areas in 1997 and in the one map are very, very similar, not identical but very, very similar to the orange areas in Exhibit D1/406, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not pretend I can talk about demography because I'm not an expert, but I'm afraid that my learned friend is -- knows exactly as much as I do about demography. What I have learned in the past two days from the professor is when you ask a demographer whether things are similar, a demographer cannot say yes, it is similar. He has to talk about things with precision. In the previous answer, he answered just in the way a demographer can, because if one municipality changes over a period of one year, he can not say that things are similar. He has to be mathematically precise. We cannot deal with these subjects by using terms, "Roughly similar" or "roughly identical." That's why I believe we should all have patience and listen to what the professor has to tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness could answer this question first by saying in a layman's eyes, those pictures are roughly identical, but there is something like this, rather than come into the explanations first, so that we could not know where we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, just to move us along, I think -- I was not trying to state -- I wasn't trying to state the obvious, Mr. President, but I think everyone in the courtroom can compare the two maps and they speak for themselves. Let me follow up with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would ask this question to be answered. If this is not done, I will ask it once again in my redirect. A question was asked. I would ask my learned friend to either withdraw his question or let the witness answer it, or else I'll have to put it in my redirect. And with your permission, to continue, Your Honours, this argumentation is in fact futile. Everybody agrees that these are similar maps to a certain degree, to a lesser degree, but then why are we guessing when we have the expert witness here who can tell us whether the maps are similar, how similar, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Counsel just indicated that the point that I just made a moment ago. Everyone in the courtroom can see that they are quite similar, so I withdraw my earlier question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, looking at both of these maps, both your D1/406 and Exhibit P947, wouldn't you agree with me, sir, at the area marked on your map in bright orange on the -- along the border of Croatia in Herzegovina and what is similarly marked in the bright or the dark blue colour in 947 would you agree with me, sir, that those boundaries look extremely similar to something called the Croatian banovina?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got a clue how the Croatian banovina looked like. I never had a map of the banovina, and I wonder whether anybody ever had a map of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, we have had maps in this courtroom. Are you telling us, sir, that why your professional career as a demographer, you've never seen a map of the banovina?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember ever seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in both your direct examination, your direct testimony, and in your report, there seems to be -- you seem to make some point of the fact or the assertion that a number of Muslims in fact lived and continued to live in West Mostar, the HVO controlled part of Mostar, during the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My question to you, sir, if you can assist the Chamber with this, what do you suggest -- what do you suggest these Muslims living in West Mostar should have done? They were cut off from the outside world, were they not? In terms of getting to what might be called ABiH-controlled territory? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only think aloud about it but I don't think I have been invited to do it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me just maybe abbreviate the questions this way: You're not suggesting, are you, that they should have gone into East Mostar, which is being shelled and was short of food and water and medicine, and that should have gone from West Mostar voluntarily to East Mostar, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this expert witness is not a fact witness here. My learned friend had such witnesses before, and everybody knows it seems to me, for what purposes this expert witness was invited to come here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. In this aspect, I agree with Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just point out to the Chamber that I submit to you that there is an attempt in his report and in his testimony to make somehow make some point that -- and I assume it's that well, things couldn't have been so bad in West Mostar because many Muslims remained living there during the war, and I simply am cross-examining on that point. I'm move on and I submitted to the Chamber that it's not clear exactly what the suggested alternatives were. But I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor has agreed to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in several of the delegations or bodies that you were involved in during your time in -- roughly the 1992, 1994 time period, on several occasions, you were working closely with a man named Anto Valenta; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You didn't work with him first during late 1992 and in early 1993 and then later again in 1994?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard about him before, and after that I saw him, and I heard him, but only on television or on radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, wasn't Mr. Valenta one of the vice-presidents of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna? And a close associate of Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can provide no reliable answer to that, under any circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall that Mr. Valenta published a book in 1991 titled, "The partition of Bosnia and the struggle for integrity this," in which he argued that the solution to the ethnic problems in Bosnia-Herzegovina was a partition of Bosnia along ethnic lines?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, when, on this single occasion I worked with him, I saw the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, if I could for the record purposes the title of the book ends with integrity, I just notice there is the word "this" in the quotation mark. The title is, "The Partition of Bosnia and the Struggle for Integrity." Full stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you had worked with him at least on this one occasion and you had seen the book at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. On a single occasion, while we were working together, preparing the Vance-Owen Plan. I thought this needed to be added.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you ever use that book as a basis for any of the work you did?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'd just like to return to your background for a few minutes. You've stated in your -- the report that was provided to us as part of the background, you had published, I think you said it again yesterday, you had published -- you've published several books and studies and approximately 130 scientific and professional works; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says in my CV, and I insist on that to be correct information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You also state that you have edited a large number of books, anthologies and magazines. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was editor -- now, what is large number of books, of course, is a relative term.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you acted in a role as editor, for example, what kind of work did you do? What was your work or role as an editor in the occasions when you -- perhaps it's different for different people but in the times when you've told us you edited a large number of books, anthologies and magazines, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did something that is typical for an editor all over the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And please describe that to us.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which specific example should I use?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Whichever one you'd like to, sir. Do you recall any of the particular books that you published or, excuse me, edited and any of the particular authors that you worked with?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was editor, for example, of a proceedings of works published as a follow-up of a scientific meeting held towards the end of 1994 in the town of Neum. The meeting was called, "Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Objectives and Possibilities." This conference was participated by around 250 intellectuals who discussed a variety of topics there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, my point is a current -- is not to get into a discussion of that conference, but I simply ask you to describe to the Chamber your role as an editor and you said you wanted a specific example, but can you just assist us please in the role that you played? Did you collect information? Did you verify information? Did you what we might call spell check? What did you do as an editor?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as usually, whenever scientific conferences are held, people are invited to attend who have their scientific contributions to make. Usually at such a conference you submit your contribution or paper. Then the paper is exposed to a debate and it -- at the end, the editor needs to, together with a board, to make sure that the papers and the results of the discussion are published in a proceedings and of course, must make sure that the works are edited, are examined scientifically, and then the proceedings are published and sent to the scientific public at large. The editor usually participates in the scientific and technical preparations for the meeting concerned, as well as is put in charge of drafting such proceedings, as is usual in international conferences. So in the course of this war, it was easier to be an editor than it had been before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, well let me just build on that to ask you this: Did you consider important in that role as an editor, did you consider it important that the material that you prepared, and ultimately edited and in some sense approved, that that was accurate and reliable information?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, in science, everybody is held accountable for whatever they did, they wrote, and thought, and obviously, I'm also held responsible for sometimes for what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just ask it this way: Would you lend your support or give your name to a publication as either an author or an editor if you felt that information or publication was unreliable or false in some way?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is usually the author who is responsible for his publication. I'm not a know-it-all to be able to judge everybody. We know in terms of standards what are the responsibilities of the author, of the reader, the scientific reader, and the editor. Therefore, all mistakes or unreliable or false statements made are to be accounted to the author.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well let me ask -- let me direct your attention to a particular author, do you recall working for a time with a man named Karlo Rotim, R-O-T-I-M?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recall the first and the family name, but not the man that I worked with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of work Mr. Rotim is involved in?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Rotim, I've noticed it from his books, of which I was the scientific reader, two of them I read and approved as a scientist, well, he is a student and a researcher of social circumstances. He is an author of orthographs, of tourist guides and similar publications and during the war, he collected information and facts and published them in the manner which he chose to be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you consider him to be a conscientious and reliable author or producer of works, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way. My experience with him is only with these two books, and they both have the same title, as far as I can remember, the title was, "The Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what was your opinion or assessment as editor of the reliability of those works?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid, once again, that notions are here a problem. In fact I was not the editor. I was the scientific reviewer of the text. The editor is usually appointed by the publishing house. I was usually just a scientific reviewer to -- and my responsibility was to scrutinise the methodological concept of the publication offered and suggest for publication.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me for using the wrong terminology. In your role as a scientific reviewer, did you find Mr. Rotim's work to be reliable?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to establish that Mr. Rotim prepared a series of documents that have to do with a specific period of time and a specific territory, area. I thought that he, in his capacity as a historian, who had published a few books before, had both the need and felt the need to publish the documents that he was able to compile and that he was able to publish. He thought that these documents should be conveyed to further generations. Of course, the documents he chose, he chose on the basis of his own criteria. But I can tell you that he is a very solid compiler of information and documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I'd like you to turn to page 2 of your report, if you have it there in front of you. I'm afraid I'm going to have to refer I'll be referring to the pages in the English version. But if you turn to page 2, or -- sir, there is a statement in that -- on that page, and at least on the English version, it's toward the bottom -- it's at the bottom of page 2. And your report says this: "There is no internal stability either, following an unfinished war, parenthesis, not the first time in this area, close parenthesis, which was ended by an imperfect peace. Indeed the 'torture by Dayton' of this international protectorate continues." What do you mean, sir, and can you assist the Chamber in explaining what you mean by a "unfinished war"?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very simply, this simile, metaphor can be construed that this war was interrupted by a peace agreement. Fortunately, I'd add.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, were you suggesting at all that the war was unfinished in the sense that it was not allowed to go to certain conclusions that perhaps might have been more favourable to the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just told you my opinion, and I insist on this opinion. Fortunately, this is how it was. I was never thinking along your lines, the lines that have also been indicated through your other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Can I ask you to look, please at page 9 of your report? And in the first paragraph that begins on that page, you state that "thus according to the 1991 census, 317.923 persons born in Bosnia-Herzegovina were registered as permanent residents of the Republic of Croatia and among them were 193.346 Croats or 25.4 per cent of the total number of Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991." Can you tell us the significance of that information? By including that in your report for the purpose of giving it to the Judges in this case, it wasn't clear to me the point you were trying to make about the fact that so many of these people were registered as permanent residents of the Republic of Croatia as opposed to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, unfortunately, I cannot find that page, but I can still answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to tell you what demography and a demographer are interested in? If you allow me to do that, then obviously in every population covered by demography, we will notice shifts which are due to natural causes, such as deaths and births. Then migration, that is immigration and emigration, and unfortunately, also due to sporadic, and talking about my country, this happened three times in the past century, they have a major impact upon population shifts, particularly the three wars I have just referred to. Direct, indirect impacts, demographic, non-demographic impacts, because after all, the war causes casualties, causes demographic injuries as well, through refugees, killed persons, displaced persons, et cetera, and a war ravaged territory is certainly not an area in which demography could have the fortunate role of studying these population shifts. As mentioned yesterday, when trying to answer the question how and what impacted upon the development of the population in the -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina, whereby averages have to be ignored, I tried to find out what happened to the total population there, and to the individual three peoples. In this context, the sources that are available are very few, because official statistics are not always published in terms of the population in its own country, let alone in the other countries. So this statement illustrates my conclusion that the Croats, whose number in the 1991 census was as mentioned before, in fact show that this country was ethnically cleansed in peace through national migrations in which both Croats and Serbs participated. So did the Muslims but not to such a high degree. Being a demographer, I was able to procure a lot of inputs for other scientific disciplines to study these phenomena should they be interested in them. My way of thinking, however, is the one you have just heard. After all, demography is a subject taught at faculties and departments of sociology in American universities. This is why I included this in my report, and it's quite possible that the figures contained have relevancy to other questions and issues as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir. I won't pursue that further, given the time, but if I could direct your attention to page 11 of your report --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have certain difficulties. It's very difficult for me to compare the pages of both versions in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your pagination is different than mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I appreciate that, sir. I'll read it. That's one of the reasons I'm reading it out loud. I'm sure if I read something incorrectly from your report, that someone in the courtroom would correct me. But on page 11 of your report, sir, you say this: About the middle of the page: "In other words the Croatian demographic ebb was simultaneously balanced by the Muslim demographic flood. Thus without this type of approach, it is impossible, within the stated biodynamic course of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to establish the correct diagnosis which reveals in this country's biological life biological energy of the Muslims and the depletion of the Croat population already falling behind biologically, the most affected by emigration." I'll stop there. I know we are coming up to break time, Mr. President, I believe, but I'll try to finish on this one particular item. Can you tell the Judges, sir, what you mean by -- in reference to the Muslims having biological energy? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that my colleagues, demographers, sometimes have problems with my very colourful style of writing. Every person has his own style, every person has his own method. I'm not very happy with your translation into English, because it is indeed very difficult to translate my words, my language, into English, because my language requires more poetic expression. I'm used to living in a multi-ethnic environment and I am always very aware of all the differences. I have selected relatively acceptable demographic terms and notions in order to give some colour to very boring statistics, and the boring statistics show those components which affect the changes in the overall population are portrayed in a more romantic way but still accurately. The differences in the growth of population which result from birth rates, mortality rates, immigration, emigration an unfortunately wars, result in the differences in demographic trends, which in turn work in new quantitative relations, and exert influence not only on birth and mortality rates but on the overall social system, including the economic, political, social, psychological systems, and that's why I thought we should look at all the different trends, which in such very sensitive -- demography is a social science and its social purpose is to respond to the question whether there are any collisions on those grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, let me -- I'm trying to finish up here before the break on this point. Let me also, then, as you did, use different terminology, perhaps less romantic, perhaps more layman's terms but is your observation or assertion here, sir, that the Muslims were having -- were and are having more children than the Croats? Is that what you mean by "biological energy"?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, but that is not the result of either religious, national or other reasons. I do not support Malthusian theory. I support the theory of demographic transition which puts the development of the population into socioeconomic context, and in the context of historical changes. We are talking about the national structure of a country struck by sufferings based on the 1991 census and we forget everything that happened ten, 20 or 30 years before that, not to mention the things that happened long time ago. That is why it is very important to put demography within the context of social development, because the data, the percentages, will not speak for themselves. They have to be interpreted by demographers. If statistics were enough, demography would not exist. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. The demography and statistics would not exist without economics. Economy would not be necessary if -- if people could live just from the air that they breathe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can break there, if you wish, and I would tell the Chamber that hopefully with some cooperation from the witness, I would expect to finish well within the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will break until 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if I could ask you to turn to -- again, I realise it's difficult to have the page references, I don't even have, to be clear, sir, I don't have a Croatian language version so I can't even direct you to it if I could. Otherwise could. But on page 17, again I'll read it to you. Top of page 17 of your report, it says, "All those who intend to supply an 'even simpler formula,' for this tragic corner of Europe through its 'integrity,' 'unity,' 'cantonisation' as such, without a quote multi-, multi-, multi-, are engaged in an useless pursuit." Now, can you tell the Chamber, sir, please what did you mean by those who pursue something along the multi-, multi-, multi-? Why was that an useless pursuit?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely refuse that my text has purported to do something like that. As individual, as an intellectual, I believe in the possibility just opposite to the one that you have just read to me. But looking at the specific society, I find in it a lot of reasons for what I have written. I believe that a society is not a summer cottage that you will build overnight. It takes time. When I was giving my testimony yesterday, and when I mentioned that half of the population in Bosnia and Herzegovina were illiterate at the beginning of the 1950s, of the last century, I also mentioned that at the time half of the people in this country was illiterate and heavily encumbered by the tragedy of the Second World War and that the way this society had been built had to be based on different considerations, because the tragedy that struck the country in the 1990s was not innate only to these people and only to the country from which I come. That would be my shortest possible answer to your question. What it says here is correct, but this is the way I understand what is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if the witness could please be shown Exhibit -- excuse me, because I'm skipping over a few things -- Exhibit P940? Sir, this appears to be an article that you wrote or published titled, "The demographic Cascade of the Croatian Archipelago in Bosnia-Herzegovina, To Stay or To Go." And again, I only have what was off the internet, English version, let me direct your attention, I'll read a particular portion to you, please, on page -- it's on page 6 of the English version. I'll make sure?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. [Interpretation] I don't know whether there is a Croatian version. We only have an English version. I do not object. I just want to say that my learned friend said English version. Is there a Croatian version? If there is, can we have it? If not, I do not object. I just want to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Counsel, if I misspoke, I apologise. The only version that I found on the internet that we found on the internet was the English version. I did not have a Croatian version. If I did, I certainly would provide it to you. At least it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, you may read that paragraph to the witness so that the interpreter could help you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, just so I'm not inconsistent, Mr. President, let me just note, and I see it now, frankly for the first time myself, that at the end of this document, internet, there seems to be a Hrvatska Budnica -- some sort of connection, interlink, internet connection so I may be inaccurate on that, frankly that's the first time I've seen that, but I will read the one passage, the single passage that I will put to the witness is on page 6. It says, "These interests --," I'm looking at the first full paragraph, starting on page 6. "These interests include securing, geographic transit, economic, cultural denominational, traditional and other relevant presumptions in order to transform unfavourable conditions to favourable conditions." Sorry, my apology. "To transform unfavourable conditions to favourable conditions for living in one's own historical domain." I'm going to skip a part of it in a moment but it goes on to it say, "We must also consider the fact that these Croat areas benefit," et cetera. Mr. President I'm now going towards the end of the paragraph, last couple of sentences from the end of the paragraph, where it says, "We must know and understand our destiny and take it into our own hands." Sir, what did you mean when you said here that the Croat people in Bosnia-Herzegovina should take destiny into their own hands?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I must say that what you have given me, as far as -- allow me to show you. My first name, my last name, and the title of the work, I know. But the rest of it, I see for the first time. The Croatian version exists here in the courtroom. We can, if need may be, take it and give it to the Honourable Chamber. In the book --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Professor, if we have it, can you please tell us where it is? We will give it to the interpreters so that they can read it. Take the contents of the book and look at the demographic cascade. Are you referring to this book here?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Croatian demographic cascade in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in brackets,"To Stay or To Go." This was published. It is written in pencil in 1993 or 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please ask the usher to assist me and give the professor the book so he may locate the paragraph he will probably find it easier than me. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Yes. I've found it. The chapter is called, "Persecutions and the allusion is to the political schemes which always in any war end up in a tragedy." And my concern is reflected in the title, but my title more poetic and speaks about the people who is also my people. This was published in the -- journal "Croatian Song," in Mostar in November, 1994. I repeat, in this book, you can find it, and as far as I know, I've learned from the Croatian cultural society, Nopridak, from Sarajevo, you can also find it on their internet page. Allow me, if I may, to refer to question, Mr. Prosecutor. You were interested in my opinion on the text that you have read to me. I was thinking about the answer, so unfortunately I did not hear the number of the page so that I could now locate the quoted paragraph. It is not going to be very easy because, again, the translation does not reflect my style of writing, but still, I would have to locate that paragraph in order to be able to answer your question, because in addition to the solemn declaration that I took here, I also have an obligation as a scientist to explain the things that I have written. Please assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I can't assist you with the Croatian language version because I do not have one, nor could I read it. It is on page 6 of the English version. It is in a section that's numbered, it's immediately above a section number 3, "War and Croats." So perhaps if you could find the section number 3, "War and Croats," you can use that as a mark. And then go further up the page until you see that language.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay, okay, okay. [Interpretation] That's the last paragraph in the previous chapter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I take some time to read this paragraph? You would help me by allowing me to do this. I would find it easier to concentrate. This is nothing new. This has been before the general public for a long time, but I have forgotten it. This was some seven or eight years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to cut you short, sir, but because of the interests of time, let me direct your -- let me direct you to one other part of that document, which, given the choice of time, I'd rather direct your attention to, please, because I can see it's going to take a long time to deal with that paragraph. If you --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a document. This is just my scientific contribution which was published in a professional paper, and then republished in this book in two languages, the Croatian and the English. This is my scientific point of view, my position, as a scientist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for clarifying that this is your position. If I could direct your attention to part 4 of this report, publication, whatever word you'd like to use, part number 4, first paragraph, this is the paragraph that starts in the English translation "through an awareness of the strategic, it says -- I'm assuming "goals," but I don't want to interpret. But it's that paragraph, in any event, "Through an awareness." Do you find that, under heading 4? Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, but my subtitles are not numbered. So that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... move on.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever published it on internet --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the second sentence starting in that paragraph, sir, says this: "If Muslims do not understand that the life of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina is connected to the Republic of Croatia by an umbilical, then there is no room to question whether Croats, in parenthesis, Croatia, end parenthesis, lost Bosnia. In this case, the main objective becomes connecting the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the Republic of Croatia, a system of tasks that must be accomplished," et cetera. Was it your position, sir, you've just told us this paper states your position, that the federation that resulted from Dayton, the Muslim-Croat part of Bosnia-Herzegovina should in fact be joined to the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, my version, in my own language, is completely different. If I can remember the Dayton Accords did not take place in November, but December, of 1994, and this was written and submitted to the magazine in July or in August of that same year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, you claim that your version, in your own language is completely different. Would you please read that paragraph and let the interpreters help us to understand how different it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with pleasure. "This that is so --" that's the second sentence of the second paragraph, "then we would have to reprogramme the interests of the then Croatians of the Republic of Croatia and of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. What we are dealing here --"

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, excuse me [Previous translation continues] ... perhaps that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm looking at the first paragraph under item number 4, if your heading isn't numbered, do you have the heading that says, "How to raise the floodgates to prevent the Croat departure"? Do you have that heading?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's right in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Skipping the first sentence starting with the words in English, "Through an awareness," the second sentence of that paragraph, I'll just read the first couple of words again to see if we are on the same paragraph then I agree with Mr. President that that's the way we should proceed, "If Muslims do not understand," now, can you find those words?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that the second sentence? "If Muslims accept that the life of the federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina," it is not "understand" but "accept".

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As the President directed you, sir, read that sentence out loud so that the interpreters can translate it to us in English so that we can see if there is in fact any material difference in what we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "If Muslims accept that the life of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina is connected by an Umbilical cord and depends on the Republic of Croatia, then there is no reason to doubt or to question whether Croats or Croatia have lost Bosnia. In that case, there is a -- one main objective and that is to join the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the Republic of Croatia, and create such a system of tasks which have to be carried out, and instruments by which they will be implemented."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. That's as far as I had read to you. If I can just ask your assistance one last time, in the beginning of that paragraph -- the beginning of that sentence, just the first five or six words I'm not sure we were once again following the same passage. "If Muslims," can you just start with that first part?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The awareness of the strategic role of Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina, especially in the area where they are more densely present, is the most natural background for a long-term establishment of the geopolitical stability of the Croatian state."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you read the next few words as well? In the next sentence?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Again, as again, in that case, there is a main objective, to join the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the Republic of Croatia and --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the next sentence is, "If Muslims do not understand," at least according to my English version. I think you read something like, "If Muslims accept that the life of the Federation of Bosnia." Would you please read this sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are right, Your Honour. "If Muslims accept that the life of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina is connected by an umbilical cord and really depends on the Republic of Croatia, then there is no room to question whether Croats, as a whole," that's what I would add now, "And the Republic of Croatia have lost Bosnia."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, and the question that was based on -- based on all that or connected to it all that long process was: It is your position that it was then the main objective or should be the main objective of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina to become connected to the Republic of Croatia? And that was the position you stated in 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, this is the position that I have taken over from the Washington Agreement which served to stop the war between the two peoples, that later on were joined in the federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, and again I'm cutting -- Mr. President I'm cutting -- I can tell the Chamber through a substantial amount of -- out of material. But let me ask you this, sir. In your report you repeatedly used the terminology that we talked about earlier this afternoon such as biological, forgive me I don't want to misquote you. Biological energy, the Muslim demographic flood, and let me put it to you, sir, isn't that rhetoric very similar to the rhetoric that, for instance, the Serbs and Bosnian Serbs used to incite racial strife and violence against the Muslims, that there was a demographic time bomb and these Muslims were going to take over the country? Isn't that exactly the same rhetoric that was used by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I have tried to explain how I perceived these notions, these terms, and I told you that it never occurred to me, and I reinforce that message, that it never occurred to me to purport something like that, because as a human being, as a member of one people, as a person who has lived there for a long time, I have my own pride for not having any such thoughts. There may be an error in the language, in the understanding, in the style, but my intention was never the way you portrayed it. I would like to be able to speak in shorter terms but this is not part of my profession. I'm a demographer and I have to seek to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. present the boring statistics in a more acceptable and a more understandable way. Every people has its own biology. People are born, people die, within a social context. Facts only make sense if they are put within a context. And that is also true of the sentence that you have just read to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance to distribute to the witness and to the courtroom Exhibit P927/2? Sir, I've just handed to you an excerpt of one of the books by Karlo Rotim that you say that you assisted with, you said you worked with him on two books. Two books. It's correct that it was two volumes, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to my learned friend for interrupting him. The witness has been explaining for half an hour to the Prosecutor what his task was in connection with this book, and he was very clear in stating that he had nothing to do with the accuracy of these texts and now the Prosecution is submitting these texts and is wasting our time. Perhaps we are even going to read these texts, for which the witness, in advance, emphasised that he had nothing to do with them, and he at great length explained what the role of a scientific reviewer was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I disagree with counsel's -- the testimony will certainly speak for itself. The think the role indicated by this witness, and -- and his view of the author as being a reliable producer of such work, is more substantial than counsel just indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That all depends on what kind of question you're going to put to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, sir, you've indicated that you were involved with Mr. Rotim concerning two books, and they were -- it was a two-volume set, number one and number 2, titled, "The Defence of Herceg-Bosna." Wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I did not work with Mr. Rotim. I worked on my own, reviewing this book. Mr. Rotim himself, and on his own, prepared his book.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And on the -- you can direct -- you can certainly direct your attention, if it assists you, to the Croatian version attachment but you are listed on the first page or what would be perhaps the beginning cover pages, internal cover pages of the book that most of us would be familiar with as one of the reviewers, professor doctor Ante Markotic, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard about this before the break, yes. This is what I said, and I can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you're listed as reviewer and other people are listed as language editing and proofreading, somebody else is interested or other persons, excuse me, are listed as computer layout, and you're listed as reviewer, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct, for the third time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I'm only going to take your attention to a couple of passages, of course the Chamber can look at the document more widely, but if you turn to the -- what would be for you, sir, the third page of the Croatian language version under the heading, "Professional units," and below that, "Convicts Battalion."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Prosecutor has been using the cross-examination for something he has been confirmed 100 times so far. Namely that the reviewer has nothing to do with the text and the author who is only an exclusively responsible for it. This is now being read out and submitted to sort of abuse cross-examination. For 100 times, this witness had explained it to you. Your Honours, the Prosecutor cannot interrupt me while I'm talking, with your permission, of course. This is a classic abuse of --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. President, I don't have any choice. Let's excuse the witness. We can't have this discussion in front of the witness and then ask the witness about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will not debate on this very issue. In my jurisdiction, an expert witness should be unbiased witness. That is he only comes here to testify on specific technical or scientific issues which is in his field of expertise. Mr. Scott, we understand this witness came here as a demographer. That is his field. So if you are going to ask some questions about some population statistics in this book, you are allowed, but as to the contents of this book, we believe it has nothing to do with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness, if I can respond, to make a record on this, the witness has indicated extensive involvement in publications, something like 130 articles, he's acknowledged working with Mr. Rotim on this book, contrary -- I respectfully submitted to the Chamber that contrary to what counsel was saying a few moments ago, he indicated much more greater involvement and responsibility for this work, and I'm happy to go back and pull up the transcript if we need to. That it was a responsibility of every person, I think, was very close to his words, every person involved in such a project, to be -- take steps or be as sure as possible, reasonably possible, that a work is accurate and reliable, to put your name to it associate your name with it and I specifically asked him would you associate your name with any work that you did not find to be reliable or problematic or fraudulent in some way and he said of course not. Now, further --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, let me finish making my record on this. In addition to that, Rule 90(H)(2) Provides specifically this: I'll wait for you to find that, Mr. President, (H)(2), in the cross-examination of a witness who is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party, counsel shall put to that witness the nature of the case, to the party for whom that counsel appears, which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness. That's one point. That's one step. There is also, Your Honour -- excuse me, Mr. President, my apology. There is another part of the rule, Mr. President, and I admit that at the moment, I'm not going right to it, but clearly in examination of witnesses, the rules provide, I hope to find it in a moment, that also when a witness is present, has come to The Hague and is able to give relevant testimony on something beyond the scope of his perhaps direct examination, he may be allowed to do so. And I would indicate to the Chamber, if we are not allowed to do this while Mr. Markotic is in The Hague on this occasion, then we will seek to call him as a Prosecution witness. We will call him back on this subjects. This is highly relevant. I know that counsel apparently wants to object to this evidence but this witness has shown a strong connection to this publication and it is appropriate to put simply a couple of questions to him, and if we are not allowed to do it now we will seek to recall him as part of the Prosecution rebuttal case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, as I understand the rules, Rule 90(H)(2) is applying to the ordinary witnesses, not to the expert witness. I believe that an expert witness is called and his testimony should be limited to the fields he's familiar with, he's an expert in that field. I quite understand that the document you showed is relevant to this case. We have no doubt about it. But at this moment, this witness is not going to testify on that issue. It is so decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, then as I say, we will seek to recall him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are not going to debate on this issue. This Court has made a ruling already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I simply inquire, then, is the Court satisfied that the record has been made that, in fact, this professor, Ante Markotic is the same professor who did act as the reviewer of this publication?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course, we have already noted that and this witness gave testimony in this aspect. It has been registered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you want to tender this document, we would like to consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will move on. I appreciate the Court's ruling and of course I will abide by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, my final question or two to you is this: Isn't it true, sir, that you have been and are for, at least as of 1999, were for a separate Croat entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, in a variety of your non-demographic questions, I tried to establish a demographic context.
